title: Putting Off and Putting On
definition: Putting Off and Putting On is the biblical pattern of rejecting sinful ways and embracing new conduct fitting for life in Christ.
summary: Putting Off and Putting On describes the believer's daily rejection of the old life and practice of the new life in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ has made believers new, so they are called to put off the old self and put on Christlike character.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Putting off and putting on describes the believer's active response to sanctification: rejecting old sinful patterns and practicing new Christlike obedience. Scripture does not call Christians merely to stop sinning but to be renewed and walk differently.

Putting off means naming and forsaking what belongs to the old life. Putting on means actively embracing truth, holiness, love, and habits that reflect the new self in Christ.

Jesus has made believers new, and the Spirit renews their minds. This doctrine shows that change is both grace-driven and actively practiced.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many try to change by suppression alone. Putting off and putting on gives a fuller path: repent of what is old, renew the mind with truth, and practice what fits life in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Choose one sinful pattern to put off and one Christlike practice to put on in its place. Use Scripture, prayer, accountability, and repeated obedience rather than vague intentions.
